nothing happens. The judge is able to proceed without incident.
a child asks whether the teams are allowed to vote for themselves. The judge says no. The child asks whether bribery counts as voting.
a gust of wind blows away the scoring sheets. Both teams chase them through the village.
the Isolan team accuses the village of copying a carving technique. The village points out that it was SHOWN to them earlier. The misunderstanding is resolved after a rather awkward conversation.
one of the creations collapses. The judge pauses the contest and checks whether anyone is hurt. Nobody is injured; the damaged entry is evaluated according to the announced criteria.
the two team leaders begin arguing over which creation is prettier. The judge asks them to stop providing unsolicited commentary.
a visiting spectator offers to buy both entries. The judge reminds everyone that the competition is not an auction.

The visitors share the prize feast with the village, saying that a good celebration should include everyone.
The judge orders a second trophy made. The two teams spend the afternoon helping each other finish it.
The teams agree to display the trophy in a shared meeting place, provided nobody secretly moves it.
The leaders decide to alternate possession of the trophy. They immediately begin arguing about who gets it first.
Someone suggests cutting the trophy in half. The judge looks horrified.
The teams abandon the trophy entirely and share a meal. The judge is secretly relieved.
A wooden statue's nose suddenly falls off. Both teams swear it was perfectly attached a moment ago. The judge declares that noses were not part of the scoring criteria.
The trophy turns out to be a beautifully carved wooden spoon. The winning team uses it to serve stew.
The judge awards the prize to a small, perfectly made stool. Nobody remembers which team actually built it. After the records are checked, the mistake is corrected.
A child asks why the statue has three ears. The sculptor replies, "For better listening." The child seems satisfied.
A visiting elder declares the ugliest entry the most historically authentic. Everyone asks for an explanation. The elder says, "You had to be there."

The two team leaders sit together after the contest, comparing sore hands and laughing about their mistakes.
No grand friendship is formed, and nobody changes their beliefs. But the next time the communities meet, they greet each other by name.

invite.name: The invitation
invite.text:
An unexpected invitation has arrived at the village workshop.
"To our neighbors," it reads, "we propose a friendly contest to determine which community possesses the finest woodworkers on Isola. The contest shall be conducted with dignity, fairness, and absolutely no unnecessary boasting."
Below the message, someone has added in a different handwriting: "WE ARE GOING TO WIN."
(Builder1), the village's {most enthusiastic builder|most meticulous craftsperson|self-appointed artistic expert}, reads the invitation aloud. (Builder2) {laughs|looks offended|starts sharpening a carving tool|asks whether the other community knows what it has gotten itself into}.
The visitors arrive carrying wood, tools, and a suspiciously large banner. Their team leader greets the villagers with {a solemn bow|a friendly handshake|a dramatic flourish|an extremely competitive smile}.

judge.name: The judge
judge.text:
A neutral judging party has been invited: {JUDGE}. Neither competing community may choose the winner.
"The rules are simple," the judge announces. "Each team must create something useful, beautiful, or at least recognizable. You may choose your approach, but both teams will be judged by the same standards."

choices.label: Ask the Isolan team to agree on a few shared safety rules first.
Propose a friendly exchange of techniques before judging.

precise.text:
The village team measures every board and checks each joint. (Builder1) insists that even the smallest mistake could ruin everything.
The Isolan team, meanwhile, {works in near silence|sings while carving|uses an unfamiliar but effective technique|finishes suspiciously early}.
By the end of the allotted time, the village's creation is {sturdy and elegant|technically flawless but rather plain|so carefully measured that the team ran out of time to decorate it|beautifully symmetrical except for one extremely noticeable leg}.

creative.text:
(Builder1) declares that the village will make something no one has ever seen.
The team produces {a magnificent carved bird with moving wings|a chair shaped like a giant coconut|a wooden fish with a hidden compartment|a detailed model of the island|a statue that appears to be judging its judges}.
The Isolan team {looks genuinely impressed|tries not to laugh|immediately begins adding more decorations to its own entry}.
Unfortunately, {one decoration falls off|the creation is too large to fit through the doorway|the paint has not dried|the object makes an alarming squeaking noise whenever it moves}.

safety.text:
The village team proposes that both sides inspect their tools, agree on work areas, and keep spectators away from flying wood chips.
The Isolan leader {agrees readily|acts insulted until a loose board nearly hits (isoleader.him/her)|suggests an even better arrangement}.
The work proceeds {smoothly|with a few petty arguments|under the watchful eye of the visiting judge}.
The teams finish their creations without serious incident.

exchange.text:
Before the contest begins, (builder1) shows the visitors a clever way to join two pieces of wood. The Isolan leader responds by demonstrating {a beautiful carving technique|a clever wooden hinge|a method of smoothing rough edges|a way to bend thin wood without breaking it}.
The two teams learn something useful, then remember they are supposed to be competing.
"Don't think this means we're going easy on you," says the Isolan leader.
"Wouldn't dream of it," replies (builder1).

v1.text: The village team wins for excellent workmanship. The Isolans congratulate the winners, though one mutters that the judging criteria were clearly invented by people who love straight lines.

v2.text: The Isolan team wins for artistry and originality. The village team is disappointed but asks how the visitors made such intricate carvings.

v3.text: The judge declares a tie. Both teams are proud until they discover there is only one trophy.

v4.text: The judge declares the village entry more practical and the Isolan entry more beautiful. Neither team can agree which compliment is better.

v5.text: Both entries fail the required safety test. The judge refuses to reward an unsafe object merely because it looks impressive. The teams must repair their work.

v6.text: The judge admits that both creations satisfy different purposes and awards separate prizes under the announced categories.

v7.text: The judge selects a winner, but both teams accuse the judge of having terrible taste. They then agree to accept the decision after reviewing the scoring notes.

repair.name: The repair round
repair.text:
The teams have one hour to repair their entries. The village team {reinforces the joints|replaces a broken leg|removes a dangerous splinter|starts again with a simpler design}. The Isolan team {tightens the supports|repairs a cracked panel|removes an unstable decoration|borrows a tool with permission}.
The judge {awards the safer finished entry a narrow victory|declares a draw|decides neither entry meets the standard}. Nobody is seriously hurt. The teams gain a great deal of respect for careful workmanship.

show_end.name: The shared showcase
show_end.text:
The judge announces that both communities have made something worth celebrating. The villagers place the entries side by side.
Some admire the Isolan patterns. Others prefer the village's construction. A few children care only about the wooden toys.
For the rest of the afternoon, the two communities exchange stories, techniques, and increasingly exaggerated accounts of how difficult the contest was.
